definition: A form of model parallelism that splits individual tensor operations (like large matrix multiplications) across multiple devices, rather than splitting whole layers.
details: Tensor parallelism allows very large individual layers, which don't fit in a single device's memory, to be computed collaboratively across multiple devices, complementing pipeline and data parallelism strategies.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Here is the short version: A form of model parallelism that splits individual tensor operations (like large matrix multiplications) across multiple devices, rather than splitting whole layers. The part that makes it sing: Tensor parallelism allows very large individual layers, which don't fit in a single device's memory, to be computed collaboratively across multiple devices, complementing pipeline and data parallelism strategies. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Tensor Parallelism — is what makes everything else possible.
